sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A group calling itself the Department of Peace accessed and leaked details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security personnel. Distributed Denial of Secrets published the database, named Icepick. Outlets disagree on exact numbers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, citing nearly 6,600, about 6,600, 7,000, or roughly 10,000 records. gist: A second fatal high-speed train collision in Spain has killed at least 69 people.
Leaked audio suggests computer and human errors caused the crash near Urda.
The disaster has intensified political pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez before elections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Renfe train rammed a stationary Iryo train from behind on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, killing at least 69 people. The disaster follows a rail crash in January that killed 46 people. Leaked control-room audio suggested a computer failure and human error caused the collision.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The tragedy occurred a month before a snap general election, disrupting political campaigning across Spain. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his transport minister, Óscar Puente, face heavy criticism over rail safety. Conservative and far-right opposition parties have used the disaster to attack the government's management of public infrastructure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Spain's main train drivers' union, Semaf, called a strike to demand that safety be prioritised over travel urgency. Opposition politicians are demanding accountability, while Vox has urged the Supreme Court to investigate Puente. Rail safety is expected to dominate the upcoming general election campaign.

gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike released her first statement following a botched execution.
Pike reported experiencing continuous physical pain, mental suffering and medical complications after surviving.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused executions while an independent review investigates the failed procedure.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Christa Pike survived a failed lethal injection on 30 September in Tennessee. Execution staff spent nearly an hour attempting to establish an intravenous line to administer pentobarbital. Pike spent ten days in intensive care suffering from pneumonia, severe swelling and swallowing difficulties before returning to a rehabilitation centre infirmary. She subsequently released a statement describing constant physical pain, mental anguish and isolation, whilst criticising official incompetence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pike is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection execution attempt. The botched procedure sparked widespread international shock. Slemmer's mother described the execution as a mess and demanded an apology, whilst the Tennessee Department of Correction defended its execution method.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the rest of the year and ordered an independent review into the botched event. Lee indicated that Pike's death sentence will remain unchanged unless court rulings determine otherwise.

gist: Google booted up its Project Suncatcher satellite to run AI inference tasks in orbit.
The spacecraft used an onboard Gemma 4 model to generate a space-themed haiku.
Testing will evaluate how radiation and thermal stress affect chip performance in space.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Google successfully booted up its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, which launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Using the onboard Gemma 4 model, the satellite generated its first response, a space-themed haiku, alongside telemetry prompts. The spacecraft carries four Tensor Processing Units, though power limits allow only one to operate at a time.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The project explores whether data centres can operate in space to process distributed AI workloads. Orbit exposes hardware to thermal stress and cosmic radiation, which can trigger bit flips in memory and corrupt data. Google aims to test whether inference workloads remain viable under these real-world conditions rather than ground simulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Google will test how the processors withstand orbital conditions before launching two interconnected satellites in 2027. Those future spacecraft will feature higher power generation and optical links.

fivew: Google conducted the experimental satellite test.

The spacecraft is operating in orbit in space.
The test aims to evaluate processor performance under radiation exposure and thermal stress.

sections.text: A study published in Science Advances found 107,356 plant and animal species in use or traded globally, which is more than twice previous estimates. Researchers used comprehensive datasets and tracked species sold online for decoration and pets.

gist: Canada and the EU announced a new Alliance for the Future.
The partnership aims to counter geopolitical unpredictability and economic pressures.
Canada agreed to contribute to a support loan for Ukraine.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Canada and the European Union announced a new partnership called the Alliance for the Future during a two-day summit in Montreal. The alliance is open to like-minded countries and aims to offer stability, reduce trade and travel restrictions, and lead to an integrated market. Canada also agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine and join Europe's supercomputing network.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The alliance serves as a hedge against unpredictable geopolitics, climate emergencies, and the weaponization of trade. It addresses concerns over reliance on American companies and defense technologies, while seeking to build certainty around supply chains and lower the cost of living for families.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further discussions will lead to a more integrated market and new educational opportunities. A clearer scope regarding Canada's potential associate membership is expected to be decided at a 2027 summit.

quotes.text: Our societies have been shaken by new storms
We have the ambition, trust, and creativity to shape it together.

timeline.text: Why does the legend of Sawney Bean and Scotland's cannibal clan persist?

gist: The legend of Sawney Bean tells of a Scottish cannibal family.
First recorded in 18th century England, the tale's historical accuracy is disputed.
The myth influenced popular culture, horror films, and tourism attractions globally.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: According to the legend, Sawney Bean moved with a woman to a coastal cave in South Ayrshire. Their family grew to dozens, murdering and eating travellers on the highway between Girvan and Ballentrae. Eventually, King James and four hundred men hunted down the killers, who were captured, taken to Leith, and executed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts suggest the story originated as sensationalised fan fiction during a time of anti-Scottish sentiment in England. Some historians believe the tale was created to degenerate Scots as barbaric. While experts like Dr Gordon McKelvie doubt Bean ever existed, locals like Chris Campbell argue the descriptions suggest he existed in Galloway, where myths may have protected smugglers.

fivew: Sawney Bean, his family, King James, and various commentators.

Scotland, specifically associated with the South Ayrshire and Galloway coasts.
The story endures by appealing to a primal fear of human capability and a desire for lurid tales.

gist: Human rights lawyer Arnon Nampa received a cumulative sentence of over 34 years in prison.
His offence was violating Thailand's strict lèse majesté law by questioning the monarchy in 2020.
The law has been used extensively against student protesters, leading many to flee into exile.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Arnon Nampa, a human rights lawyer, was sentenced to a further prison term under Thailand's lèse majesté law, bringing his total sentence to more than 34 years. He was prosecuted for a 2020 speech where he dressed as Harry Potter and called for public scrutiny of the monarchy.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The law has been used in hundreds of prosecutions since 2020 to smother public discussion about the monarchy. Courts interpret the law broadly, and defendants face severe sentences and difficulties mounting a defence.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Dozens of activists remain on trial or have fled into exile to avoid imprisonment. Arnon faces pending verdicts in additional cases and may spend his entire life in prison.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Donald Trump and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February, triggering wider conflicts involving Hamas, Hezbollah, six Iranian militias, and the Houthis. The conflict disrupted global shipping and pushed worldwide inflation to 4%, while Saudi Arabia faced severe economic contractions and a ballooning budget deficit. Amid plunging poll numbers and rising fuel prices, Trump attempted to deflect blame toward Ukraine, demanding Volodymyr Zelenskyy stand down and restricting Ukrainian access to Starlink.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The interconnected nature of global conflicts means that US interventionism has sparked cascading crises, undermining stability in the Middle East and threatening peace worldwide. The resulting economic squeeze has alienated European leaders, who increasingly view US policies and tech monopolies as an existential threat to their sovereignty and political survival.

sections.text: A study published in Science revealed that Manx shearwaters get jet-lagged when flying across time zones on foraging trips. Because they navigate using the Sun and their internal clocks fall out of sync with local time, they veer slightly off course.

sections.text: The navigational errors reach up to around 15 degrees, adding only a few extra kilometres to their journeys. Understanding how birds manage this could help researchers design bio-inspired autonomous navigation systems and potentially offer insights into mitigating jet lag in humans.

The trust implemented post-operative changes following an investigation into the preventable death.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eleanor Hazel Aldred-Owen, aged 21 months, died on 2 October 2023 after routine surgery at Alder Hey Children's Hospital. An investigation identified 24 care failures, including an unflagged abnormal chest X-ray and untreated collapsed lung, causing cardiac arrest and brain injury. A coroner found she died of misadventure contributed to by neglect.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Alder Hey Children's Hospital NHS Foundation Trust accepted full responsibility for gross neglect following a long process. Her parents expressed unbearable guilt and trauma, while their solicitor stated the family placed their trust in the hospital and were let down.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The hospital trust has introduced changes, including two post-operative procedures named after Eleanor, which her family hope will keep care safer for other children.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Experts discovered Short-Necked Oil Beetle larvae at Castlemartin Range in Pembrokeshire after three years of searching. Only dead adults were found at the site last year, but the discovery of larvae suggests the species is breeding in Wales again after 60 years.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Poland's prime minister, Donald Tusk, vowed to push through a contested overhaul of the constitutional court during a television address. President Karol Nawrocki intervened by entering the building, while the European Commission urged him to approve newly nominated judges.

gist: Lenders fund neocloud firms using lease contracts and chips as collateral.
Share prices for several neocloud companies have dropped significantly over the past month.
Experts warn that neocloud businesses face high financial risk if tech spending drops.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Neocloud firms funded their expensive hardware purchases by borrowing money against lease contracts with large tech clients and their purchased chips. Recently, stock values for companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, and Applied Digital dropped notably. Lenders are asking for higher returns, and some firms have cancelled public share sales.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These smaller infrastructure providers carry heavy debt loads to fund necessary hardware. Their financial success depends heavily on massive AI developers and major tech customers continuing their high spending levels. Any reductions in tech spending or rising borrowing costs could cause severe financial distress across the sector.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Industry analysts suggest the sector may face widespread consolidation and failures among smaller firms. The future remains tied to upcoming public share offerings from major AI developers and the continued ability of neoclouds to borrow funds.

Research gathered at the launch aims to identify effective support methods for men.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Connect Outdoors, a new charity, is launching officially at the Venture Centre in Maughold during an International Men's Day event. Expecting around 80 participants, the event offers outdoor activities including hill walking, archery, bushcraft, and ice baths to encourage men to connect and improve their mental health.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Organisers argue that men's mental health services are often designed without consulting men directly. Utilising natural green and blue environments provides non-clinical settings where men feel secure to talk, helping tackle isolation and reduce loneliness through shared activities.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Event participants will complete surveys to help researchers discover which activities and approaches best engage men, shaping future wellbeing support on the island.

articles.title: English children’s homes are in crisis. Does Denmark hold the answers?
articles.standfirst: UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister has travelled to Copenhagen to see what can be learned from Danish system

timeline.text: English children’s homes are in crisis. Does Denmark hold the answers?

gist: English children’s minister Josh MacAlister visited Denmark to study its residential care system.
England’s children’s home sector faces soaring costs, falling standards, and illegal unregistered homes.
Officials aim to learn from Danish methods to reform English children’s social care.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The British children’s minister, Josh MacAlister, visited Denmark to inspect its children’s homes as part of a Department for Education review. England’s residential care system faces severe strain, with soaring expenditure, declining standards, and 669 children placed in illegal, unregistered homes last year.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Unlike England, where 83% of places are privately run, Danish homes emphasise degree-educated staff, family-like environments, and long-term stability. English teenagers often face abrupt departure from care at 18, whereas Danish residents can stay until age 23.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The UK government is considering ending the rigid age-18 exit threshold and reforming care culture. A market oversight body will be established to increase financial transparency before capping private provider profits, while local authorities work to curb demand.

quotes.text: We need big changes, a major shake up
But we can learn from it.

articles.title: ‘Progress takes time’: Stonewall CEO on turning down the heat on the trans debate
articles.standfirst: Leader is charting a course through troubled waters as a new survey finds trans people feel more pessimistic about social acceptance after combative decade

timeline.text: ‘Progress takes time’: Stonewall CEO on turning down the heat on the trans debate

gist: A Stonewall survey shows 58% of trans people feel less accepted than a decade ago.
Stonewall chief executive Simon Blake calls for calmer debate following a supreme court ruling.
Gender-critical campaigners say the ruling clarified that legal sex means biological sex.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A survey by LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall found that 58% of trans+ people feel less accepted than ten years ago, with 80% pessimistic about equality. The findings follow a UK supreme court ruling stating that legal sex means biological sex. Stonewall chief executive Simon Blake said trans people fear retreating from public spaces. Gender-critical campaigners welcomed the ruling as clarifying existing law.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Many trans people report avoiding spaces such as public toilets, hospital wards and sports teams due to safety concerns and new guidance. Meanwhile, gender-critical campaigners argue the ruling restores protection for women's single-sex spaces without requiring case-by-case justification.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Simon Blake has called on the government to monitor the ruling's impact and address any harms. Stonewall is not seeking to overturn the ruling but is exploring how to ensure trans people remain protected under the law.

quotes.text: We understand that this is the law.

timeline.text: Asylum seekers still being sent to France under ‘one in one out’ weeks after scheme ended

gist: The Home Office continues deporting asylum seekers to France after the scheme ended.
Some returned asylum seekers have already crossed the Channel back to the UK.
The removal scheme cost British taxpayers at least £78 million.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Home Office is continuing to detain and deport asylum seekers to France under the "one in, one out" arrangement, despite the scheme officially ending on 1 October. A deportation flight left on Wednesday, and another flight is planned for 17 November.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood stated the scheme cost at least £78 million. Critics highlight that the policy caused severe harm to vulnerable people without deterring Channel crossings. Additionally, at least seven returned asylum seekers have already returned to the UK.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Officials are continuing returns for the remaining cohort detained under the scheme. Meanwhile, several returned asylum seekers in northern France are currently preparing to cross the Channel back to the UK.

gist: Trent Alexander-Arnold is currently third-choice right-back at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho.

Jamie Carragher suggested Alexander-Arnold made a mistake joining Real Madrid.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled for regular playing time at Real Madrid since joining in June 2025. Manager Jose Mourinho currently prefers Fede Valverde, a midfielder, at right-back, leaving Alexander-Arnold as third choice behind Valverde and Denzel Dumfries. He has featured in seven of Real's 13 matches this season, starting four times.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Alexander-Arnold's lack of regular minutes follows a difficult debut season impacted by hamstring, thigh, and muscle injuries, alongside frequent managerial changes. Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher stated that Alexander-Arnold made a mistake moving to Madrid, noting that being third choice suggests the club wants him to move on.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Alexander-Arnold hopes for more playing time during Real Madrid's three upcoming fixtures before the international break. Additionally, England manager Thomas Tuchel must decide whether to include him in the next England squad, announced on 6 November, for Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

articles.title: England see off USA to return to winning ways

timeline.text: England see off USA to return to winning ways

gist: England returned to winning ways with a victory over the United States in New Jersey.
Claudia Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries as England exploited space out wide.
The United States displayed impressive physicality and resistance throughout the contest.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England defeated the United States 55-12 in New Jersey during the WXV Global Series. Claudia Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries, while Jones, Venner, Field, Feaunati and Kabeya also crossed the line for England. Rogers and Zackary scored tries for the United States.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The performance leaves England head coach John Mitchell with plenty to ponder regarding set-piece solidity and attacking fluency before their Women's Six Nations title defence in April. Meanwhile, the United States demonstrated strong physicality and determination.

fivew: England defeated the United States in a rugby match.

timeline.text: Returning Estevao brings X-factor to strikerless Chelsea

gist: Estevao Willian shone in Chelsea's 2-0 win over Manchester United.
Morgan Rogers scored a brilliant solo goal to break the deadlock.
Chelsea coped with key absences by deploying a strikerless formation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Estevao Willian made his first Premier League start of the season in Chelsea's 2-0 victory against Manchester United. He had two goals disallowed and received a standing ovation. Morgan Rogers scored a solo goal in the second half, and Cole Palmer sealed the win from the penalty spot.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Chelsea faced a shortage of options with eight players missing, including first-choice striker Joao Pedro. The impressive performances of Estevao and Rogers eased pressure on head coach Xabi Alonso after recent defeats and proved the team can find creative attacking solutions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Estevao's standout display will increase pressure on Xabi Alonso to keep the winger in the starting lineup for upcoming matches.

fivew: Chelsea defeated Manchester United two-nil in the Premier League.
Estevao Willian and Morgan Rogers secured the victory despite a striker shortage.

Today has worked really well

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton striker Thierno Barry's home in Greater Manchester was burgled while he played in a Carabao Cup tie against Newcastle United on Thursday. Greater Manchester Police confirmed an ongoing investigation.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The 24-year-old Frenchman voiced relief that his partner and toddler were attending the match in the stands, noting the situation could have been much worse.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Barry stated he will stop putting his family at risk by posting about his personal life and lifestyle on social media.

The League Two team advanced by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout.
The quarter-final matches are scheduled for the week starting 14 December.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fleetwood Town advanced to the quarter-finals after overcoming Arsenal on penalties. They will now face the winners of the match between Everton and Newcastle United. Meanwhile, holders Manchester City were drawn against Bradford City, Liverpool will play Bournemouth, and Crystal Palace face Sunderland.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fleetwood Town are the lowest-ranked club remaining in the tournament and have achieved a historic milestone by reaching the final eight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Fleetwood await the conclusion of the fourth-round fixture between Everton and Newcastle to discover their specific opponent. The quarter-final ties are scheduled to occur during the week beginning 14 December.
